title: Rose's name, Creole family and occupations
summary: Perhanis explains how he met Rose through the book Storyville. Rose gives his full Creole name, says he grew up in the French Quarter, and lists his interests: jazz, writing, concerts, art.

story.theme_name: Stating your name and birth date on tape
story.community_name: Opening the tape: name, birth date and birthplace

blocks.x: It's too early for me. And my name is John Perhanis, and I'm from Minneapolis, studying at the Jazz Archives at Tulane for a period of six weeks here, in which time I met Al Rose, who lives in New Orleans. And I should mention that I met him through one of his books called Storyville. Which, when I picked it up in the bookstore, fascinated me so much that I went out and bought it, which I could not afford to do, but I did anyway. And then I called Al Rose, and we got to know each other a little bit. Al, there's so many aspects of your life and work that we could go into. But one of the things I'd like to ask you about first is a little bit about your background before we get into any discussions of music or other things of your life. Maybe I ought to ask you first whether Al Rose is your real name, and maybe we can find out something about your lineage.

Well, the name itself is real, of course, but it's much truncated. My full name is H.N. Alphonse Delarose Lascaux, and it is, as you might suspect, an old New Orleans name. And I am myself a representative of the seventh generation of the family in New Orleans. Is that a Creole, of Creole? Oh, yes. It is a Creole name.
And is Al Rose a pen name, as it were?

Well, from the Alphonse and Delarose, I eventually derived it because I was looking for something much shorter to be able to use efficiently. But anything that I have written, almost anything I have written, has been under that name.
Now, you were born in New Orleans, of course.
Yes, grew up in the French Quarter. Grew up in the French Quarter.
All right, now, can you tell me what your occupation is?

Not really, because I'm frequently asked what my occupation is. And my occupation is mainly not working. But I have a lot of things that interest me, which I have been pursuing for a lifetime, among which are jazz, writing, the production of concerts, and, of course, I'm a professional artist, and anything else that strikes me as I go along.
